analysis_sections.text: The transformed portrait keeps parts of the eyes, mouth and head outline recognizable, while shifting other appearance into coarse textured bands. It can be compared directly with the original face and the surrounding formal scene. This is a display of graph filtering, not a photograph of a generation artifact; the detector’s spectral branch operates on learned features, and the signed contribution view provides a separate model readout.
analysis_sections.title: A transformed view of the same face

analysis_sections.text: In the middle displayed pair, a strong positive readout lies on the viewer-left side of the lower central face grid, with positive support elsewhere in the face. The distribution changes across sampled pairs. These signed values explain support for the fake-minus-real classifier margin. They should be kept distinct from the compact attention proposal and from claims about the video’s production method or a specific visible texture defect.
analysis_sections.title: Where the classifier readout supports its decision

analysis_sections.text: The unsigned learned map proposes a compact central facial focus, partly overlapping the cheek-related contribution pattern. It comes from a separate head trained on frozen detector features to identify useful explanatory patches. The connected selection summarizes that focus for inspection. Its presence is informative about the explanation head’s proposal, while signed contributions and recorded interventions provide the separate evidence about classifier direction and regional response.
analysis_sections.title: The explanation head’s proposed focus

analysis_sections.text: Some recorded comparisons favor the central selected region, while others favor the strongest matched controls. The complete regional criterion is therefore not met. The experiments still help describe how hiding and restoring this particular input region affects the detector. This gives the portrait a measured local evidence profile alongside its strong classification score, rather than treating a realistic original image as proof of either class.
analysis_sections.title: What the selected-region measurements establish

report.conclusion: The integrated model assessment is manipulated; the calibrated detector assessment and signed readouts establish the direction, with regional evidence described separately.

diagnosis.evidence_synthesis: The wider shot shows a realistic-looking seated speaker and coherent local gestures. Classification strength comes from the calibrated detector score, with positive facial grid readouts explaining its direction. The attention proposal overlaps part of that response but does not qualify under every regional comparison. This is a model-grounded diagnosis of the portrait rather than an inference about its identity or production method.

classification.rule: Strong: predicted-class score at least 0.90; moderate: at least 0.70; borderline: below 0.70. Descriptive display bands, not an independent accuracy estimate.

regional.rule: Intervention-supported requires all eight recorded whole-curve comparisons and source, fidelity and stability checks in every displayed clip. Failed localization does not change the video classifier.

inherited_editor_changes.after:
A bearded man in a dark shirt sits at a desk in a green chair, with flags, framed pictures and lamps in the background. His hands stay clasped as his mouth and head move slightly across the short windows. The formal interior and realistic-looking presentation provide useful context for a detector assessment that is not explained by an obvious visible defect.

SSTGNN favors manipulated with strong predicted-class support under the display policy. Positive readouts occur in facial grid locations near the cheeks, and learned attention proposes a compact central region. The recorded region measurements are mixed. These views describe the model’s response to the portrait without identifying the person or inferring how the video was produced.
